When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **3/10** (WARNING, price action mostly calm) vs VIX Spike Tier **4/4** EXTREME, **85%** probability
Price signals are lagging and options are forward-looking, because skew, backwardation and the adaptive trigger are all active. Trust the VIX Spike Detector for near-term risk, since options traders price the move before the Crash Index registers it.
⚠ These two disagree: S&P 500 **+1.3%** over 5 days, QQQ and SPY correlation drift **+0.88 -> -0.16** vs Composite divergence zone TOPPING, **74.4%** of pairs diverging
A rising index with fraying internal relationships is how late-stage advances look. Trust the divergence read for fragility, but the price trend for direction until it breaks.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **40** (ACCUMULATE, partial signal) vs Regime state **61** (TRANSITION) with MIXED bias and a TOPPING divergence zone
Dip-buying signals and topping signals can't both lead. The contrarian score is only partial at **40**, so trust the topping evidence and wait for a fuller signal before adding.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

Stress is building beneath a calm surface, and you should treat it as real. The Crash Index reads 3/10 and the S&P 500 gained +1.3% this week. The VIX Spike Detector is at 4/4 with an 85% probability, and 74.4% of tracked pairs are diverging.

That gap is the story. Price still shows a market that holds together, while options and cross-asset relationships show hedging demand and a broken internal structure. The regime score of 61 (TRANSITION) and macro state CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence say the same thing: gains sit in a few leaders while the Russell 2000 slips -0.4%.

For positioning, you cut gross exposure into strength and keep hedges on rather than chase the index. The contrarian score of 40 offers only a partial buy signal, so keep dry powder and build slowly on weakness. Favor liquid, large-cap exposure over small caps and crypto, where SOL fell -8.5% in 5 days.

The main risk is a volatility spike that hits before the Crash Index catches up. The stance flips if VIX backwardation fades and the Crash Index stays at or below 3. It turns more defensive if the Crash Index climbs toward 5 while the Russell 2000 keeps falling.

Macro Regime — where are we structurally
AI read · macro regime

The regime is CONCENTRATION at 55% confidence, which is a modest conviction. The regime score of 61 sits in TRANSITION with a MIXED bias, so the market hasn't committed to a direction.

In a concentrated market, a few leaders carry the index while most stocks fall behind, and the Russell 2000 at -0.4% fits that. Position around the leaders you already own, keep size moderate, and avoid broad small-cap exposure until breadth improves.

A rise in regime confidence well above 55% toward another state, or the Russell 2000 matching the S&P 500, would change the call.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means assets that normally move together are splitting apart. Correlation drift is the change in how tightly two assets track each other, measured from an older reading to a recent one. The composite zone is TOPPING, with 74.4% of 43 pairs diverging and 27 bearish against 5 bullish.

The sharpest breaks score 80 each. QQQ and SPY went from +0.88 to -0.16, so tech no longer moves with the broad index. KRE and XLF slid from +0.24 to -0.70, which means regional banks are decoupling from financials. AUDJPY fell from +0.41 to -0.24, a risk-appetite warning. NVDA and AMD flipped from -0.84 to +0.29, and XLE and XLK moved from -0.72 to +0.30. The jaws score of 100 is the maximum. Markets that rise on loose internal links tend to break when one leg gives way. A re-tightening of QQQ and SPY would calm this read.

The 24/7 tape is split, and the US is the middle ground. Asia is led by the Nikkei at +4.9% while the Shanghai Composite lags at -2.8%, so strength is Japan-specific.

Europe is flat to weak, with the SMI at -0.2% and the CAC at -2.5%. The US leads on the S&P 500 at +1.3% but small caps trail at -0.4%.

Crypto is the weakest risk gauge: BTC fell -3.7% and SOL -8.5%. Crypto trades through the weekend and often shows risk appetite first, so its weakness says speculative demand is fading.

For today's US session, expect large caps to hold up while small caps and speculative assets stay under pressure. A crypto rebound would soften that call.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 3/10 · WARNING — 3+ signals, active surveillance
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index and the VIX Spike Detector disagree, and that's a coherent state. The Crash Index sits at 3/10 because it scores price damage that mostly hasn't happened yet. The VIX Spike Detector reads 4/4 EXTREME with an 85% probability because the options market is already paying up for protection.

Three triggers are active at once: skew, backwardation and the adaptive trigger. Backwardation means near-term fear costs more than later fear, which is how markets price an imminent move. Trust the options reading for timing, since it moves first. The Crash Index tells you damage hasn't started, and the VIX tier tells you the market expects it. A Crash Index jump past 3 while backwardation persists would confirm the move is underway.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 3/10 — a few early signals are stirring; watch whether more line up.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read

Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
